text: Fire runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the big ask you make before fear catches up, the quiet party that comes alive when you walk in, and the bid you raise because someone else wants the same prize.

You wait to feel ready rather than work to be ready, and getting ready never ends. Preparing is the part you control, and you choose another round of it over a first attempt. You are allowed to start before the feeling arrives.

Protecting the people you love is the first thing you do with news. Because you treat their safety as your job, you protect them from a risk rather than watch them take it. You are allowed to stand beside them and let the risk be theirs.

Spreading yourself thin feels safer than betting on one thing, and it keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. You run all of them on the one body you have.

Saying too much proves to you that you have something to add. Since a held tongue feels like a wasted turn, you spend your standing on the extra line instead of the needed one. You talk away trust that comes back slower than it left.

When a rule stops making sense, you rewrite it with people still standing on it. Since you fix it rather than keeping the peace, you change the footing with no warning. The rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.

Shutting people out feels like rest to you, and you reach for it more than you need. Your own company works so well that you mistake it for the plan rather than a break. You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time.

Paying for everyone feels like winning to you, even when the money is shared. You would rather cover the whole bill than split it, and you use savings meant for two. Along with the money, you spend a plan you made together.
You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, because your standing feels at stake. You replay each defeat for weeks after the game is over.

Your best thinking happens alone, and you go off to it without saying how long. Thinking best out of reach, you let the solo hours run on and lose track of the clock. The people waiting on you never know when to expect you back.
Saying no has never come easily to you. A yes keeps the evening warm and everyone pleased, and you agree before you check what it costs. You never had to buy your place with a yes.

Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You would rather have a good time now than keep a promise later, and you spend the shared money on the evening. You leave them short on the plans you made together.

You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, and you would rather do badly in front of people than well on your own. Remember that you are just as real with no one watching.

Before others find their words, you have already spoken up for them. Speaking comes more naturally to you than waiting, and you take the floor rather than hand it over. The quieter ones get heard in your words more than their own.

Losing stays with you far longer than winning does. A rival's win feels like something taken from you, and you set out to get it back. You turn every friendly game into a fight and miss the fun of playing.

Beside someone you like, you are all in unasked. You would rather add your own money than ask if they wanted it, and you double what they put in. Your money makes their plan bigger and riskier than they chose.

The care you give so freely is also the care you lean on in return. Because another person's steadiness feels more reliable than yours, you lean on theirs rather than build any. You go without the one kind of strength you cannot borrow.

Your own needs come last whenever you are looking after someone. Being needed feels better to you than being rested, and you give your evenings away rather than keeping any. Your hobbies, friendships and plans all wait their turn behind everyone else's.

You are harder on yourself than anyone else has been. Letting a mistake go feels like letting yourself off, and you go over it long after everyone else has moved on. You paid for each mistake the first time, and that was enough.

Staying on duty is how you love the people in your care. Watching over them comes easier to you than sitting with them, and you stand guard where they wanted company. You keep them safe and miss the evenings they hoped to share with you.

Fire runs through your career, your health and your growth. It is the hard week that wakes you up, the body that finds its second wind when the stakes are real, and the deadline that gets more out of you than you planned to give.

You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes before enjoying the thing. Underneath the counting, you want to enjoy what you have.
You hold back hardest where you love most. You keep a reserve rather than give it all, and your partner gets the careful share only. You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see.

Asking comes last, well after the point where it would have worked. Owing anyone feels like losing ground, and you carry the whole load instead of sharing it. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load.
Doing it alone is where your strength shows. You trust your own hands before anyone's plan, and you finish what others are still waiting on. What you build is yours from the first nail to the last.

When a sprint would get you there, you keep your own pace instead. Being late on your terms sits better with you than being rushed on someone else's. Some doors shut while you are still walking towards them.

Your biggest bets land on other people too. Going big matters more than going safe, and that puts the shared money at your size of risk. You set the size of a risk that the people who pooled with you have to carry.

Thinking a question through means thinking it around, each side first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You circle a question for weeks that a single choice would have closed.

You are spread among more things than your body keeps up with. Because letting go feels like losing rather than choosing, you keep all of them and reach each one worn out. Spread this thin, you never get a full rest and start each day already tired.

Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Because helping them out feels better than keeping, you spend on their short weeks rather than a shared cushion. You spend the savings that would have seen all of you through a lean month.

Leaving comes hard to you, and you stay where the giving back stopped. You have more Wood than strength for it, so you stay rather than face what leaving costs. You keep paying in effort every month to a place that returns none of it.

You put comfort first for those in your care too. You would rather see them happy now than stretched, so you pick pleasant hours over useful ones. You trade the effort they would grow on for an hour of ease.

Looking far comes naturally, and it pays. The next place is clearer to you than this one, so you notice the far chance more than the near one. The opening right in front of you is the one you walk past most.

Finishing is what you save for later. The last stretch costs you more than the first, and you would rather open a new thing than close an old one. You leave the money and the credit sitting at the end you skip.

Tired, you shut people out before anything else. Quiet is how you recover, and you would rather shut people out than ask for the quiet you need. You only ever wanted rest, never distance from the people you love.

Spotting openings is what you do before anything is obvious. Carrying less Wood than drive to spend, you notice the far chance more than the one in your hand. Half the good ideas in your circle started as something you pointed at.

With money, you would rather spend than let it sit. Since spending feels like living and saving like waiting, you spend the whole month instead of keeping any. You pay for the free spending with savings you never get to keep.

You change in front of an audience, for the better. Being watched is where your focus comes from, and you would rather perform a thing than practise it. Your best work happens live, and the crowd gets all of it.
What you make comes out without strain. Ease is the sign you trust, and you would rather do the thing that flows than force the thing that counts. Your work has a lightness people feel at once.

You make hard things look easy. You would rather show the finished thing than the work, and you leave the people learning from you the ease without the steps. Anyone watching you sees how good the result can be.
